rationale.usefulness: Typed Choice, Score and Noul outputs and exposed distributions are directly useful for routing, ranking and review queues (ts-intro; ts-confidence). Proposed teacher workflows are actionable but explicitly untested.
rationale.impact: A meaningful approach to embedding semantic judgments in ordinary software, with potentially broad routing and classification applications (ts-intro). Acquired evidence does not establish field-wide transformation, superior real-world accuracy or learning gains.
rationale.novelty: Native typed questions, distribution outputs and shared-state composition provide a distinctive integrated interface (ts-intro). These support meaningful differentiation, not proof that classification, probabilities or programmatic orchestration are newly invented; 1.14 itself is an incremental update.
rationale.maturity: Detailed versioning, confidence definitions, context and rate-limit documentation support a usable text API (ts-models; ts-confidence). Jev 1.14 is currently preview, new modalities remain experimental, and no independent reliability test was acquired (ts-114).
rationale.openness: Documented primitives, formulas and version IDs provide some interface inspectability (ts-confidence; ts-models), but this evidence establishes hosted access rather than open model weights, local execution or reproducible training. Vendor-controlled service and experimental headers constrain portability.

concerns: Non-blocking: official-source spot checks on 2026-10-18 confirmed release date, experimental scope, aliases, price, context and confidence formula. These are vendor documentation, not an API execution or calibration experiment.
The source reference table labels standard input Text while the release enables images behind an experimental header; these scopes are compatible and the report preserves that distinction.
